source.title: Exploring Scaling Laws of CTR Model for Online Performance Improvement
source.authors: Weijiang Lai; Beihong Jin; Jiongyan Zhang; Yiyuan Zheng; Jian Dong; Jia Cheng; Jun Lei; Xing-Xing Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and figure text are flattened, but the paper is identifiable and the relevant sections are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law experiments to CTR models, a different setting from language-model pretraining. Its results concern CTR AUC, not language-model held-out cross-entropy loss.
record.gate_note: The paper tests AUC against model size, sequence length, and sample count for CTR models; it does not measure language-model pretraining loss, language-model parameter/token/compute scaling, compute-optimal allocation, or downstream language-model performance. The AUC scaling results are recorded as findings outside the listed claim versions. The online A/B test and distillation results concern CTR deployment, not the listed language-model claims.
record.test_reason: The study fits saturating power laws to held-out CTR AUC against non-embedding parameters, behavior-sequence length and sample count for recommender models. That is a scaling result in a non-text setting, so it bears on V5. The measure is AUC, not cross-entropy loss, so it is a loose analogue of the LM law. V1–V4, V6 and V7 concern language models and are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also claim the AUC scaling spans three orders of magnitude in model grade and data size. They say increasing data gives a higher AUC ceiling and faster growth than increasing model grade, although the fitted data exponent γ is smaller. They present distillation as letting a deployable model benefit from scaling, with +2.81% CTR online.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits power laws to CTR AUC rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy loss. Its model grade combines non-embedding parameter count and behavior-sequence length; it does not study language-model training compute or optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: CTR AUC scaling is examined across sequence lengths, model sizes, sample counts, and model/normalization configurations; fitted coefficients vary across these settings and models.

fits_no_version.finding: CTR AUC follows saturating power-law fits in behavior-sequence length, an axis with no LM counterpart among the versions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recommender CTR AUC scales as a saturating power law in user behavior-sequence length.

record.problems: The scaling analysis uses CTR AUC rather than loss. The scaling-law experiments are conducted on the industrial dataset; the paper notes public-dataset size limitations. The figure-extracted fit formulas are flattened, so the assignment of individual formulas to sequence-length/model-size settings follows the order of the listed settings and fit formulas.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted under the row limit. CTR online A/B-test and distillation outcomes were excluded because they do not measure any listed language-model scaling version.

untested.parts: No language models or LM pretraining loss are measured.
No extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs is tested.
No shape comparison at a fixed parameter count.
Loss is not measured, only AUC. Image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested. There is no compute axis and no out-of-sample extrapolation.
No test of LM fitting choices or LM curve shape.

missing.what: Size-2 AUCs for SUAN (0.7098), Variant F (0.7092) and Variant G (0.7097). These are needed as the within-variant scaling baselines for r14 and r15.
AUC rising with model grade for SUAN-1/2/3 (0.7133, 0.7146, 0.7168) and with sequence length under sparse attention.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's not-tested call for V5 is overridden: a CTR recommender is a different modality, and its AUC fits bear on whether power-law scaling carries over, with the AUC-versus-loss caveat. The 'three orders of magnitude' claim is overstated: parameters span about 1.6 orders and samples about 1.8. The authors' 'faster growth rate' wording conflicts with their smaller exponent. All fits are in-sample, with few points per curve and no uncertainty on the fitted coefficients.

versions.untested_parts: No language models or held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss are measured.
No small-run fits are tested against much larger language-model runs.
No fixed-compute language-model allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
The study does not compare language-model architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.
The study tests CTR AUC scaling, not whether the same language-model loss law holds in other modalities or training regimes.
No downstream language-model tasks or relation between language-model pretraining loss and downstream performance is tested.

The study reports CTR AUC fits and differences among CTR models and configurations, but does not test language-model exponent sensitivity to fitting choices or whether language-model curves depart from a single power law.

rows.note: The text says AUC adheres to the fitted power-law function across different sequence lengths. Sequence-length/formula pairing follows the order of the tested lengths and fit list in the figure text.

rows.subject: Variant F (SUAN with Layer-Norm replacing RMSNorm)
rows.size_stated: size-4; exact non-embedding parameter count is not stated for this variant.
rows.stage_stated: CTR prediction; trained three times under each configuration.
rows.operation_detail: Compare AUC across model sizes after replacing RMSNorm with standard Layer-Norm.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations are reported as ±0.00331 for Variant F and ±0.00128 for SUAN.
rows.note: The authors say the size-4 variants F and G show performance degradation and attribute this to reduced training stability.
rows.check: The baseline should be Variant F at size-2 (0.7092±0.00068), not SUAN at size-4. Going from size-2 to size-4, Variant F rises only to 0.7097±0.00331, within noise. The scaling gain is largely lost.

source_check.correct: For the stated across-size operation, baseline=Variant F size-2, 0.7092±0.00068; value=Variant F size-4, 0.7097±0.00331. SUAN size-4 is a same-size architecture comparator.
source_check.problem: The baseline compares architectures instead of comparing model sizes within Variant F.

relationships.condition: SUAN, HSTU and DIN CTR models on the industrial dataset, with AUC scaled by parameters (fixed 7-day data), sequence length, or sample count
relationships.reason: Saturating power-law fits with R² of 0.95–0.999 describe AUC versus size, length and samples (r1–r4, r6–r8, r11–r13).
relationships.display_finding: Saturating power laws described AUC versus model size, sequence length and sample volume with R² values of 0.95–0.999.

source_check.reason: The study reports saturating power-law fits for these axes and models. Parameter and sequence-length sweeps concern SUAN; sample-count sweeps include all three models. Some individual formula associations remain unresolved in the extracted figures.

relationships.condition: Long sequences (length 1000) or the largest models (size-4/5); fixed data size
relationships.reason: Exponents swing widely, from 0.06 to 0.66 for size and 0.15 to 1.32 for length. Trends nearly flatten in r5, r9 and r10, and AUC saturates near 0.72 at fixed data.
relationships.display_finding: Size exponents ranged from 0.06 to 0.66 and length exponents from 0.15 to 1.32, with nearly flat trends and AUC saturation near 0.72.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Long sequences (length 1000) or the largest models (size-4/5); fixed data size
source_check.reason: The cited curves retain the fitted power-law form. V5 does not require identical exponents or unbounded AUC improvement; saturation and small positive exponents do not establish a scope failure. The specific condition-to-formula pairings are also unverified.

relationships.condition: Architecture variants with LayerNorm (F) or post-norm (G) instead of RMSNorm with pre-norm
relationships.reason: From size-2 to size-4, F stays flat (0.7092 to 0.7097) and G declines (0.7097 to 0.7064). Scaling depends on the normalization choice (r14, r15; Table 5).
relationships.display_finding: AUC barely changed with LayerNorm, from 0.7092 to 0.7097, and declined with post-norm, from 0.7097 to 0.7064.
